keyword: how long will it take for artemis to reach the moon

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission of NASA's Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'NASA’s Artemis II is the first crewed mission of the Artemis program'; R2: 'Coming more than three years after the uncrewed Artemis I test flight, Artemis II will mark the first time humans have traveled beyond low Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state Artemis II is the first crewed Artemis mission, following uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to take approximately four to five days to reach the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'it's roughly a four-day journey to the far side of the moon'; R9: 'the Orion capsule will reach the moon in five days'; R4: 'it will not be until day six of the mission... that the Artemis II crew will reach the neighborhood of the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly support 4-5 days or day 5/6 to lunar vicinity, matching 'approximately four to five days'.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II will enter the lunar vicinity around day five.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R9: 'the Orion capsule will reach the moon in five days, by Monday night'; R7: 'On day five, the Orion will enter the lunar sphere of influence'; R4: 'day six of the mission... reach the neighborhood of the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently indicate day 5 or 6 entry into lunar vicinity, directly supporting 'around day five'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will last roughly 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the mission is slated to last about nine and a half days'; R2: 'a more than 600,000-mile, 10-day journey'; R3: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe the mission as about 10 days or 9.5-10 days, directly matching 'roughly 10 days'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will fly around the moon before returning to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the plan is to loop around it'; R2: 'lunar flyby'; R4: 'whip around the lunar far side'
verifications.reasoning: Every source confirms a flyby or loop around the moon without landing/orbiting, then return.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission includes crewed travel to the far side of the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'loop around it, getting an unprecedented view of the far side of the moon'; R2: 'fly by the far side of the moon'; R5: 'trip around the “dark side of the moon”'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state travel to/around/view of the far side with crew.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will travel at speeds up to 24,500 mph (39,400 km/h) to escape Earth's gravity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Escape velocity—or the speed Artemis II will achieve to free itself of the orbital pull of the Earth—is 24,500 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Exact speed match for escape from Earth's gravity during translunar injection.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will slow down before being pulled in by the Moon's gravity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'planetary gravity steadily pulling the ship backwards until it has slowed to just 3,400 mph. It is only when the ship is about 41,000 miles from the moon... that the steadily increasing gravitational pull of the moon will take over'
verifications.reasoning: Directly describes slowing due to Earth's gravity before Moon's gravity dominates.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will take the crew 252,000 miles from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'set a record for the farthest distance humans have ever traveled from Earth: 252,000 miles'; R7: 'about 252,000 miles into space'
verifications.reasoning: Exact distance cited for maximum separation from Earth.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will set a record for the farthest humans have traveled into space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'expected to travel farther from Earth than anyone before them'; R3: 'expected to send the crew farther from Earth than any previous human mission'; R7: 'travel "farther from Earth than any previous human mission"'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm it will exceed Apollo record (e.g., 248,655 miles).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II return trip to Earth is expected to take another three to four days after one pass around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'roughly a four-day journey to the far side... and another four days back'; R2: 'three-day return trip'; R4: 'homeward trip will take in excess of 96 hours'; R5: 'process that will take up to four days'
verifications.reasoning: Sources support 3-4 days return after flyby, with minor variation covered by 'three to four'.

verifications.claim: The projected Artemis II mission timeline is scheduled for April 2026, as noted in the CBS News update and NASA official blog.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1 (CBS News): dated 'April 1, 2026' with launch updates; R3 (NASA blog): 'Live launch day updates... April 1, 2026' with 'Artemis II lifted off... at 6:35 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: R1 (CBS) and R3 (NASA blog) are live updates confirming April 2026 launch timeline.
